subject: ORION - AZ1 sustained latency & 5xx surge — exec priority and geo-redirect ask
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@orion.ai
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00Z
Subject: ORION - AZ1 latency + 5xx spike — initial alert

Team —

Orion (Prod: orion-main) is reporting a sustained latency increase in AZ1 starting ~08:50 UTC and a rising 5xx rate (~3%->18% over last 25 min). Customer-facing dashboards show error pages for a subset of requests and retries are amplifying QPS. Orion is a high-touch account (reserved throughput + SLOs). They flagged an outage to their CTO and asked to escalate to execs if we can’t mitigate within 90 minutes.

Can we do an immediate short triage and propose a geo-redirect + temporary model pin to a lower-latency variant? Priority: (1) stabilize customer traffic, (2) provide clear timeline and compensation ask, (3) loop execs only if we need cross-region authorization or credits.

Attachments: orion-az1-traces-20260816.txt (ops traces), orion-impact-summary-20260816.pdf (customer screenshots).

Marcus
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@orion.ai
Date: 2026-08-16T09:28:00Z
Subject: Re: ORION - AZ1 latency + 5xx spike — initial alert

On 16 Aug 2026 09:12, Marcus Lin wrote:
> Team —
>
> Orion (Prod: orion-main) is reporting a sustained latency increase in AZ1...

Quick triage: AZ1 interconnect to model-serving pool shows elevated queue depth and a KV-cache eviction storm for a hot prefix. Early signs point to an index-bloat from recent customer workload causing serialization pressure on the serving runtime (specific to quantized model variant). We’re seeing the following:
- Worker restart churn on 3/12 nodes (OOM-ish)
- KV cache thrash for sessions pinned to AZ1
- Upstream DB (customer-side) retries adding to tail latency

Immediate mitigations in progress (ops):
1) Increase instance concurrency cap and enable short prefix-cache TTL rollback (reduces KV churn) — 15 min estimate.
2) Initiate soft geo-redirect for new sessions to US-WEST-2 (graceful drain of AZ1) — requires routing auth from Vanessa for traffic shift >20%.
3) Provision a lower-memory model variant in US-WEST-2 to accept overflow traffic (warmup in 8-10 min).

I’ll start the shard drain and post live metrics. If Vanessa can approve the geo-redirect, we should reduce customer errors quickly.

Hannah
Sr. SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Lisa Park <lisa@orion.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: ORION - AZ1 latency + 5xx spike — initial alert

Thanks Marcus + Hannah —

We’re seeing the same on our side: ~18% error rate for interactive endpoints and user sessions failing validation flows. This is impacting our payment flows (high severity). Our CRO is on the line and asked for a call with your execs if this isn’t contained within 60 minutes.

Two asks from us right now:
1) Please provide a concrete ETA to route >30% traffic out of AZ1 (and whether you will do an automated redirect or require our config).
2) We will need an indication of crediting/discount for the breach window if the error rate persists >2 hours.

We’re available for a 15-min bridge now.

— Lisa Park
CTO, Orion Health
lisa@orion.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa@orion.ai>, David Chen <david.chen@orion.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T10:18:00Z
Subject: Escalation: Requesting exec authorization (geo-redirect + provisional credit) — ORION AZ1

Vanessa —

Summary of technical findings from Hannah: AZ1 exhibiting KV-cache eviction storm and node churn; draining AZ1 and soft-redirecting new sessions to US-WEST-2 should reduce 5xx and latency within ~10-20 minutes. Hannah estimates warmup for overflow variant in 8-10 minutes.

Customer asks for a traffic redirect ETA and a crediting signal if the incident lasts >2 hours. Proposed immediate actions requiring your authorization:
- Approve soft geo-redirect up to 40% of Orion traffic to US-WEST-2 (temporary, auto-revert after healthy metrics 30m).
- Authorize a provisional goodwill credit estimated at 15% of invoice for impacted window, to be finalized by Finance after post-incident review.
- Loop CRO/CEO only if watershed decisions required (e.g., sustained SLA breach >4 hours).

If you approve, I will confirm with Lisa and execute the redirect with ops. If you prefer to escalate to execs for authorization instead of approving now, please advise and I will add CRO + Head of Sales to the thread.

Marcus
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Lisa Park <lisa@orion.ai>
Cc: David Chen <david.chen@orion.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Escalation: Requesting exec authorization (geo-redirect + provisional credit) — ORION AZ1

Thanks for the clear summary — and Hannah for the quick triage. I authorize the following now:
1) Soft geo-redirect up to 40% of Orion traffic to US-WEST-2. Ops to monitor error-rate and latency and hold at increments of 10% if we see regression.
2) Provisional goodwill credit: authorize a 15% credit for the impacted window (subject to Finance review). We’ll include standard postmortem + credits paperwork.

Marcus/Hannah: please coordinate the redirect and confirm back with observed error-rate drop and the time we plan to revert. Lisa/David: thanks for patience — we’ll keep the bridge open and follow up with the incident report within 24 hours.

Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
